newsitem.title: USA: Minn. lawmakers call for lifting of school caps.
newsitem.headline: Minn. lawmakers call for lifting of school caps.

text.p: Democrat and Republican leaders of the Minnesota House called Monday for lifting state spending caps on schools.

In a joint announcement, House Speaker-designate Phil Carruthers, D-Brooklyn, Republican Leader Steve Sviggum, R-Kenyon and Majority Leader Ted Winter, D-Fulda, released a legislative agenda that included removal of the education budget caps.
Tom Smalec, spokesman for Carruthers, said the legislature enacted the caps in 1995 at the request of Gov. Arne Carlson, who wanted to slow the growth of state aid to schools.
However, the cap on state aid will result in a $337 million cut in funding this year and next, Smalec said.
Removal of the cap can be accomplished given an estimated $1.4 billion budget balance for fiscal 1997, which ends June 30, according to the legislators' announcement.
Smalec said a new forecast, due out in late February or early March, will be used by lawmakers for their budget resolutions.
Other areas of agreement among the legislative leaders included crafting a bipartisan plan to replace the state's current welfare system.
